notes.definition: Because monoclonal antibodies bind only to one specific antigen, they are used to diagnose conditions (such as in pregnancy tests), to measure or detect chemicals and pathogens in laboratories, to locate molecules in research, and to treat some diseases such as cancer.
explanation: Monoclonal antibodies are specific to one binding site on one protein antigen. This means they can find and attach to one particular chemical or type of cell, even when it is mixed with thousands of other substances. This property makes them useful in diagnosis, in laboratories, in research and in treating disease.

Pregnancy tests use monoclonal antibodies to detect the hormone hCG (human chorionic gonadotrophin), which is only found in the urine of pregnant women. The end of the test stick has mobile monoclonal antibodies attached to small coloured (blue) beads; these bind to hCG. Urine soaks up the stick. Further up, the test line has antibodies stuck in place that also bind to hCG. If hCG is present, the hCG with its bead-antibody attached is trapped at the test line and a coloured line appears. The control line has fixed antibodies that bind to the mobile antibodies themselves, so a coloured line always appears there if the test has worked.

In laboratories, monoclonal antibodies are used to measure the levels of hormones and other chemicals in blood, and to detect pathogens. For example, they can show whether a blood sample contains a particular virus or bacterium, or how much of a hormone is present. In research, monoclonal antibodies are bound to a fluorescent dye. When the antibodies attach to a specific molecule in a cell or tissue, the dye glows under the microscope, so scientists can locate or identify that molecule.

Monoclonal antibodies are used to treat some diseases. For cancer, the monoclonal antibody can be bound to a radioactive substance, a toxic drug or a chemical which stops cells growing and dividing. The antibody is made to bind to an antigen found on cancer cells, so it delivers the substance directly to the cancer cells without harming other cells in the body. This is an advantage over chemotherapy or radiotherapy, which also damage healthy cells.

Monoclonal antibodies also have disadvantages. They create more side effects than expected, for example fever, vomiting, low blood pressure and allergic reactions. Because of this, they are not yet as widely used as everybody hoped when they were first developed. They are also expensive to develop and produce. When evaluating monoclonal antibodies, weigh up their specificity and usefulness against these problems.
keyFacts: Monoclonal antibodies bind to one specific antigen, so they can target specific chemicals or cells.
Pregnancy tests use monoclonal antibodies to detect the hormone hCG in urine.
In a pregnancy test, the test line shows a colour only if hCG is present; the control line shows a colour if the test is working.
In laboratories they measure levels of hormones and other chemicals in blood, and detect pathogens.
In research they are bound to fluorescent dye to locate or identify specific molecules in cells or tissues.
To treat cancer, they can be bound to a radioactive substance, a toxic drug or a chemical that stops cells growing and dividing.
They deliver the substance to cancer cells without harming other cells in the body.
Monoclonal antibodies create more side effects than expected.
They are not yet as widely used as everybody hoped when first developed.

keyTerms.definition: One of many identical antibodies produced from a single clone of cells, specific to one binding site on one protein antigen.
Human chorionic gonadotrophin: a hormone found in the urine of a pregnant woman, detected by pregnancy tests.
Identifying a disease or condition, for example finding out whether someone is pregnant or has a particular infection.
A dye that glows when light is shone on it; attached to monoclonal antibodies to show where a molecule is in a cell or tissue.
An unwanted effect of a medicine, for example fever or an allergic reaction.
The line on a test stick that changes colour whether or not the target chemical is present, showing the test has worked.
A molecule, usually a protein, that a specific antibody binds to.

workedExamples.title: Reading a pregnancy test
workedExamples.question: A pregnancy test shows a blue line at the control line but no line at the test line. What does this result show? Explain.
steps: The control line contains fixed antibodies that bind the mobile antibodies, whether or not hCG is present. A blue line here shows the urine has moved up the stick and the test has worked.
The test line has fixed antibodies that only trap the mobile antibodies (with blue beads) if hCG is attached to them.
No line at the test line means no hCG was trapped.
workedExamples.answer: The test worked, and the woman is not pregnant because there is no hCG in her urine.

workedExamples.title: Explaining targeted cancer treatment
workedExamples.question: Explain how a monoclonal antibody attached to a toxic drug can treat cancer with fewer harmful effects than ordinary chemotherapy.
steps: The monoclonal antibody is made to be specific to an antigen found on the surface of the cancer cells.
The antibody binds only to the cancer cells, carrying the toxic drug with it.
The drug kills the cancer cells it is delivered to.
Healthy cells do not have the antigen, so the antibody does not bind to them and they are not harmed. Chemotherapy, in contrast, affects many healthy cells too.
workedExamples.answer: The antibody delivers the drug only to cancer cells, because it binds only to an antigen on those cells, so other body cells are not harmed.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a pregnancy test detects the baby or the egg.
misconceptions.right: In fact it detects the hormone hCG in urine, which is produced during pregnancy.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the control line only appears if the woman is pregnant.
misconceptions.right: In fact the control line appears whenever the test has worked properly, because its fixed antibodies bind the mobile antibodies whether or not hCG is present.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think monoclonal antibodies kill cancer cells on their own in the treatments described by AQA.
misconceptions.right: In fact the antibody is used to carry a radioactive substance, a toxic drug or a chemical that stops cell division to the cancer cells.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think monoclonal antibodies have no side effects because they are so specific.
misconceptions.right: In fact they have created more side effects than expected, so they are not as widely used as was hoped.

realWorld: Home pregnancy test kits sold in pharmacies use monoclonal antibodies against hCG.
Lateral flow tests for Covid-19 use monoclonal antibodies to detect virus proteins.
Hospital laboratories use monoclonal antibodies to measure hormone levels and to identify pathogens in blood samples.
Some breast cancers are treated with monoclonal antibodies such as trastuzumab, sometimes joined to a toxic drug.
higherTier: This whole subtopic is Higher tier only: uses of monoclonal antibodies (pregnancy tests, laboratory testing, research with fluorescent dye, cancer treatment) and evaluating their advantages and disadvantages.
separateOnlyContent: This whole subtopic is in separate Biology only (not Combined Science Trilogy), including how pregnancy tests use monoclonal antibodies to detect hCG.
examTips: You must know how a pregnancy test works: name hCG, the mobile antibodies with coloured beads, the test line and the control line.
When explaining the control line, say it shows the test is working, not that the woman is pregnant.
For cancer treatment, list the three things an antibody can carry: a radioactive substance, a toxic drug, or a chemical that stops cells growing and dividing.

In 'evaluate' questions give advantages (specific, only bind to target, do not harm healthy cells) AND disadvantages (more side effects than expected, not as widely used as hoped, expensive), then make a judgement.
Use the word 'specific' and link it to binding to one antigen.
summary: Monoclonal antibodies are specific, so they can target one chemical or cell type.
Pregnancy tests use them to detect hCG in urine.
Laboratories use them to measure hormone and chemical levels in blood and to detect pathogens.
Researchers attach fluorescent dye to locate specific molecules in cells or tissues.
In cancer treatment they deliver radioactive substances, toxic drugs or chemicals that stop cell division to cancer cells only.
They have more side effects than expected and are not as widely used as hoped.

questions.question: Which substance does a pregnancy test detect?
markScheme: 1 mark: hCG
questions.explanation: The hormone hCG is found in the urine of pregnant women, and the test's monoclonal antibodies bind to it.

questions.question: In research, monoclonal antibodies are bound to which substance to locate specific molecules in a cell?
options: An enzyme that digests the cell
markScheme: 1 mark: A fluorescent dye
questions.explanation: The fluorescent dye glows where the antibody has bound, showing where the molecule is. Toxic drugs and radioactive substances are used in cancer treatment.

questions.question: Which of these is a use of monoclonal antibodies in laboratories?
options: Measuring the levels of hormones in blood
markScheme: 1 mark: Measuring the levels of hormones in blood
questions.explanation: Monoclonal antibodies are used in labs to measure levels of hormones and other chemicals in blood, and to detect pathogens.

questions.question: A pregnancy test shows a coloured line at both the test line and the control line. What does this mean?
markScheme: 1 mark: The woman is pregnant
questions.explanation: A test line shows hCG is present, and the control line shows the test worked, so the result is positive.

questions.question: Why is a monoclonal antibody carrying a toxic drug less harmful to the body than ordinary chemotherapy?
options: The antibody binds only to cancer cells, so other cells are not harmed
The antibody makes healthy cells resistant to the drug
The antibody destroys the drug before it reaches healthy cells
markScheme: 1 mark: The antibody binds only to cancer cells, so other cells are not harmed
questions.explanation: Because the antibody is specific to an antigen on cancer cells, it delivers the drug only to them.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT attached to monoclonal antibodies to treat cancer?
options: A chemical that stops cells growing and dividing
markScheme: 1 mark: A fluorescent dye
questions.explanation: Fluorescent dye is used in research to locate molecules. The other three are used to kill cancer cells or stop them dividing.

questions.question: Which statement is a disadvantage of monoclonal antibodies?
options: They bind to one specific antigen
They create more side effects than expected
They can be used to detect pathogens
They can be made in large amounts
markScheme: 1 mark: They create more side effects than expected
questions.explanation: Side effects have been greater than first expected, which is why they are not as widely used as hoped. The other options are advantages.

questions.question: A pregnancy test shows a coloured line at the test line but no line at the control line. What is the correct conclusion?
options: The test is invalid and should be repeated with a new test
The hCG level is very high
markScheme: 1 mark: The test is invalid and should be repeated with a new test
questions.explanation: If the control line does not appear, the test has not worked properly, so no result from that stick can be trusted.

questions.question: In a pregnancy test, what do the fixed antibodies at the control line bind to?
options: The mobile antibodies (with or without hCG attached)
The fixed antibodies at the test line
markScheme: 1 mark: The mobile antibodies (with or without hCG attached)
questions.explanation: The control line antibodies bind the mobile antibodies themselves, so a line appears whether or not hCG is present, provided the urine has carried the mobile antibodies up the stick.

questions.question: A scientist wants to see which cells in a tissue sample contain a particular protein. What should she use?
options: Monoclonal antibodies against the protein bound to a radioactive substance, injected into a patient
Monoclonal antibodies against the protein bound to a fluorescent dye
Mobile antibodies with blue beads against hCG
markScheme: 1 mark: Monoclonal antibodies against the protein bound to a fluorescent dye
questions.explanation: Fluorescent-labelled monoclonal antibodies bind to the protein and glow, locating it in the tissue. The hCG antibodies would bind the wrong molecule.

questions.question: Name the bodily fluid tested in a pregnancy test.
markScheme: 1 mark: urine
questions.explanation: hCG passes into the urine of a pregnant woman, so the test stick is dipped in urine.

questions.question: Give two ways monoclonal antibodies are used in laboratories.
acceptedAnswers: measure levels of chemicals in blood
markScheme: 1 mark: to measure the levels of hormones/other chemicals in blood
1 mark: to detect pathogens
questions.explanation: Both uses depend on the antibody binding to one specific chemical or pathogen.

questions.question: Name three substances that can be attached to monoclonal antibodies to treat cancer.
acceptedAnswers: chemical that stops cells growing and dividing
markScheme: 1 mark: a radioactive substance
1 mark: a toxic drug
1 mark: a chemical which stops cells growing and dividing
questions.explanation: Each of these damages or stops the cancer cells once the antibody has delivered it.

questions.question: State one reason why monoclonal antibodies are not yet as widely used as was hoped.
markScheme: 1 mark: they create more side effects than expected (accept expensive)
questions.explanation: Unexpected side effects have limited their use.

questions.question: Explain why monoclonal antibodies can be used to detect one particular pathogen in a blood sample.
acceptedAnswers: do not bind to other cells
markScheme: 1 mark: monoclonal antibodies are specific to one (protein) antigen
1 mark: so they bind only to the antigen on that pathogen and not to other cells/pathogens
questions.explanation: Specificity means the antibody acts as a detector for one target only.

questions.question: Explain the purpose of the control line on a pregnancy test.
acceptedAnswers: appears whether or not hCG present
markScheme: 1 mark: fixed antibodies at the control line bind to the mobile antibodies (whether or not hCG is attached)
1 mark: so a coloured line shows the test is working / urine has moved along the stick
questions.explanation: Without the control line you could not tell a negative result from a faulty test.

questions.question: Describe how monoclonal antibodies are used in research to identify specific molecules in a tissue.
markScheme: 1 mark: monoclonal antibodies specific to the molecule are bound to a fluorescent dye
1 mark: the antibodies bind to the molecule and the dye glows/shows where it is
questions.explanation: Where the dye glows under the microscope is where the target molecule is located.

questions.question: Explain why the test line on a pregnancy test turns blue only when the woman is pregnant.
acceptedAnswers: fixed antibodies at test line bind hCG
markScheme: 1 mark: hCG in urine binds to the mobile antibodies attached to blue beads
1 mark: fixed antibodies at the test line bind to the hCG (attached to the mobile antibodies)
1 mark: so the beads are trapped and build up at the test line; without hCG the mobile antibodies pass the test line and are not trapped
questions.explanation: The test line antibodies can only catch the beads when hCG is present to link them.

questions.question: A monoclonal antibody carrying a radioactive substance is given to a patient with cancer. Suggest why healthy cells close to the tumour might still be damaged.
acceptedAnswers: some healthy cells have the antigen
markScheme: 1 mark: radiation from the substance can travel a short distance / reach nearby cells
1 mark: or some healthy cells may also carry the antigen, so the antibody binds to them too
questions.explanation: Targeting reduces harm to healthy cells but cannot always eliminate it, which helps explain the unexpected side effects.

questions.question: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using monoclonal antibodies to treat cancer.
markScheme: 1 mark: advantage: deliver the substance only to cancer cells, so other body cells are not harmed
1 mark: disadvantage: create more side effects than expected (accept expensive to develop/produce)
questions.explanation: Evaluation needs both sides: specificity is the main benefit, side effects the main drawback.

questions.question: A hospital laboratory uses monoclonal antibodies to measure the concentration of a hormone in a patient's blood. Suggest why this method is more reliable than a method that detects many similar chemicals.
markScheme: 1 mark: the monoclonal antibody binds only to that hormone (is specific)
1 mark: so other similar chemicals in blood do not bind and do not affect the measurement
questions.explanation: Blood contains many chemicals; a specific antibody avoids false readings from similar molecules.

questions.question: State what is attached to the mobile antibodies in a pregnancy test so that a line can be seen.
markScheme: 1 mark: (small) blue/coloured beads
questions.explanation: The beads collect at a line, making it visible.

questions.question: Describe some of the ways in which monoclonal antibodies are used.
markScheme: Indicative content: diagnosis, e.g. pregnancy tests detect hCG in urine; laboratories measure levels of hormones and other chemicals in blood; laboratories detect pathogens; research: bound to fluorescent dye to locate/identify specific molecules in cells or tissues; treatment of cancer: bound to radioactive substance, toxic drug or chemical that stops cell growth and division; delivered to cancer cells without harming other cells.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): at least three different uses described with some detail.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two uses named with little description.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Cover the four areas (diagnosis, laboratory, research, treatment) for a complete answer.

questions.question: Explain how monoclonal antibodies are used in a pregnancy test.
markScheme: Indicative content: pregnant women produce the hormone hCG, found in urine; end of stick is placed in urine; stick contains mobile monoclonal antibodies specific to hCG, attached to blue/coloured beads; hCG binds to the mobile antibodies; urine carries them up the stick; at the test line, antibodies are fixed/immobilised and bind to hCG; so the hCG-antibody-bead complex is trapped and a blue line forms if pregnant; if no hCG, mobile antibodies are not trapped at the test line, so no line; at the control line fixed antibodies bind to the mobile antibodies; blue line forms whether or not pregnant, showing the test has worked.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed, logical explanation of mobile antibodies, test line and control line, including what each result means.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explains detection of hCG with some reference to lines but incomplete detail on how each line forms.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, e.g. the antibody detects a hormone in urine.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: AQA requires knowledge of pregnancy tests. A full answer explains what binds what at each stage and the meaning of each line.

questions.question: Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using monoclonal antibodies in medicine.
markScheme: Indicative content: advantages: specific to one antigen, so target one chemical or cell type; quick, simple diagnosis (pregnancy tests, detecting pathogens); accurate measurement of hormones/chemicals in blood; cancer treatment delivers radioactive substance/toxic drug/chemical only to cancer cells; so fewer healthy cells harmed than chemotherapy/radiotherapy; useful in research to locate molecules. Disadvantages: create more side effects than expected (e.g. fever, allergic reactions); not as widely used as hoped; expensive to develop and produce; use of mice raises ethical issues. Judgement: very useful in diagnosis and testing, where side effects do not arise; benefits in treatment must be weighed against side effects.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed advantages and disadvantages with a reasoned judgement.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): some advantages and disadvantages, but limited judgement.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two simple points, mostly one-sided.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: An evaluation must be two-sided and end with a conclusion. A strong point is that diagnostic uses avoid the side-effect problem because the antibody is not put into the body.

questions.question: Name the type of test kit that detects the hormone hCG.
markScheme: 1 mark: pregnancy test
questions.explanation: hCG is produced during pregnancy, so tests for it are pregnancy tests.
